name: CodeFaeries QuickFind: Admin Search & Ctrl+K Command Palette
author: Long Watch Studio - Code Faeries

sections.description:
CodeFaeries QuickFind is an admin search for WordPress, opened with Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on Mac). Type a few letters in the search field of the admin bar: QuickFind finds your posts and pages, your admin menu pages, your installed plugins and your settings screens, in one list.

No more hunting through long admin menus. Type “perma” and open Permalinks. Type “woocommerce settings” and open them. Type the name of a draft and edit it.

What the admin search finds

  • Posts, pages and custom post types, drafts and scheduled posts included, that you are allowed to edit
  • Admin menu and submenu pages, filtered by your capabilities. Admin pages are listed first
  • Installed plugins, each one opening its own settings page. Inactive plugins are marked “(inactive)”
  • Core settings screens (administrators only)
  • Users, media and comments, for users allowed to manage them
  • WordPress.org plugins: the last result searches the plugin directory for what you typed (users who can install plugins)
  • Searches of several words, such as “settings general”

A keyboard-first command palette for the admin

  • Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on Mac) opens the search field of the admin bar
  • Arrow keys and Enter move through the results and open one
  • Actions on a result: the selected result shows what you can do without opening it. Activate or deactivate a plugin, view or trash a post, approve, spam or trash a comment, open a media file, list a user’s posts
  • Grouped results, with the match highlighted
  • Typos forgiven: “permalnks” still finds Permalinks
  • Choose your shortcut: Ctrl+K, Ctrl+Shift+K, Alt+K, Ctrl+/ or none. Ctrl+/ works on AZERTY keyboards too

Works with the WordPress Command Palette

WordPress has its own Command Palette, which runs commands and navigates. QuickFind does not replace it: it searches your actual content, plugins and settings. When the native palette is present, QuickFind uses Ctrl+Shift+K so the two never collide, and the search field always shows the shortcut that is active.

Settings

In Settings > QuickFind:

  • Enable or disable each search source
  • Restrict which post types are searched
  • Maximum results per group, minimum query length, typing delay
  • Keyboard shortcut
  • Search field on the public site, on or off

Everywhere in your admin, and on your site

  • On the public site: users who can edit posts get the same search field in the admin bar there

  • Phones and tablets: a magnifier in the toolbar opens a full-width search field with results

  • Your admin color scheme is followed (Light, Midnight and the others)
  • User capabilities are respected in every result

QuickFind Pro

QuickFind Pro adds more to search, on top of everything above:

  • Taxonomy terms (categories, tags and custom taxonomies) in the search results
  • WooCommerce orders and products, searched from the same field
  • An Advanced Search page under Tools: content, users, media, comments, terms, orders and products, with filters per source, sortable columns, highlighted matches and full pagination

More about QuickFind Pro

Do you like QuickFind?

A review on wordpress.org helps other site owners find it: leave a review. Thank you.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Click the search field in the admin bar, or use the keyboard shortcut: Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on Mac). When WordPress’s native Command Palette is present, QuickFind leaves Ctrl+K to it and uses Ctrl+Shift+K instead. The placeholder text in the search field always shows the shortcut that is actually active.
  3. Change the shortcut any time in Settings → QuickFind.
sections.faq:
Is QuickFind free?

Yes. Every feature described on this page outside the “QuickFind Pro” section is in the free plugin, with no time limit. QuickFind Pro adds taxonomy terms, WooCommerce orders and products, and an Advanced Search page: https://codefaeries.com/product/quickfind/

What does the admin search find?

Posts, pages and custom post types you are allowed to edit (drafts and scheduled posts included), admin menu and submenu pages, installed plugins, core settings screens for administrators, and users, media and comments for those allowed to manage them.

How do I open it?

Click the search field in the admin bar, or press Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on Mac). The placeholder text in the search field always shows the shortcut that is active.

Does it replace the WordPress Command Palette?

No. The native Command Palette runs commands and navigates; QuickFind searches your content, plugins and settings. When the native palette is present, QuickFind uses Ctrl+Shift+K so the two never collide.

Can I change the keyboard shortcut?

Yes, in Settings > QuickFind: Ctrl+K, Ctrl+Shift+K, Alt+K, Ctrl+/ or none. Ctrl+/ also works on keyboards where “/” needs Shift, such as AZERTY.

Can editors and authors use it?

Yes. Every result respects the user’s capabilities: users only see the content and admin pages they are allowed to open. Core settings screens are shown to administrators only.

Can I choose what is searched?

Yes. You can enable or disable each search source, restrict the post types searched, and set the maximum results per group, the minimum query length and the typing delay.

Does it open a plugin’s settings?

Yes. A plugin found in the search opens its own settings page. Inactive plugins are marked “(inactive)”.

Can I act on a result without opening it?

Yes. Select a result with the arrow keys or the mouse: its actions appear under it. Activate or deactivate a plugin, view, preview or trash a post, approve, unapprove, spam or trash a comment, open a media file, or list a user’s posts. Each action is the WordPress screen that does it, with the same permission checks, and trash, spam and deactivate can be undone in WordPress. Trash is not offered when your site has no trash.

Does it work on the public site?

Yes. Users who can edit posts find the search field in the admin bar there too. Admin menu pages appear on the public site after one visit to the dashboard. Turn it off in Settings > QuickFind.

Does it work on a phone?

Yes. On phones and tablets, a magnifier in the toolbar opens a full-width search field with results.

What if I make a typo?

When nothing matches exactly, QuickFind looks again with one wrong, missing or swapped letter allowed (two in long words), so “permalnks” still finds Permalinks. This applies to admin pages, plugins and settings.

Where do I get help?

On the wordpress.org support forum of the plugin.
sections.changelog:
1.2.0

  • New: act on a result without opening it. Select a result to see its actions: activate or deactivate a plugin, view, preview or trash a post, approve, unapprove, spam or trash a comment, open a media file, list a user’s posts.
  • New: the search field is also in the admin bar of the public site, for users who can edit posts. It can be turned off in Settings > QuickFind.

1.1.0

  • New: the last result searches the WordPress.org plugin directory for what you typed.
  • New: admin pages, plugins and settings are found despite a typo.
  • New: users, media and comments are searched in the free plugin. They were part of QuickFind Pro.

1.0.8

  • Improved: the plugin is renamed “CodeFaeries QuickFind: Admin Search & Ctrl+K Command Palette”, and its description and FAQ are rewritten. No change in features or behavior.

1.0.7

  • Improved: the plugin is renamed “CodeFaeries QuickFind: Admin Search & Command Palette”. No change in features or behavior.

1.0.6

  • Improved: inactive plugins are marked “(inactive)” in the search results.
  • Fixed: two installed plugins with the same name each get their own result.
  • Fixed: the Ctrl+/ shortcut works on keyboards where “/” needs Shift, such as AZERTY.

1.0.5

  • Fixed: a plugin found in the search now opens its own settings page. Several plugins of the same family (all WooCommerce or all CodeFaeries extensions) used to open the same, sometimes forbidden, page.
  • Fixed: searches of several words find admin pages, such as “settings general” or “woocommerce settings”.
  • Fixed: scheduled posts are found.
  • Fixed: a space typed at the end of a search no longer hides admin pages and plugins.
  • Fixed: the “Go further with Pro” button and the plugin site link opened a missing page.
  • Improved: admin pages are listed before content, so a search like “perma” opens Permalinks first.
  • Improved: each settings page appears once, and the General settings page is named General.

1.0.4

  • Improved: version aligned with QuickFind Pro 1.0.4. No change in features or behavior.

1.0.3

  • Compatibility: tested with WordPress 7.1.

1.0.2

  • Improved: version aligned with QuickFind Pro 1.0.2. No change in features or behavior.

1.0.1

  • Improved: version aligned with QuickFind Pro 1.0.1. No change in features or behavior.

1.0.0

First public release. Spotlight-style global search for the WordPress admin, opened from the admin bar with a keyboard shortcut.

  • Search posts, pages and custom post types (drafts included) that you are allowed to edit.
  • Jump to any admin menu or submenu page, filtered by your capabilities.
  • Find installed plugins and go straight to each plugin’s settings page.
  • Reach core settings screens (administrators only).
  • Grouped, keyboard-navigable results (arrow keys + Enter), respecting user capabilities everywhere.
  • Works alongside WordPress’s native Command Palette: automatically uses Ctrl+Shift+K when the palette is present so the two never collide.
  • Works on phones and tablets: a toolbar magnifier opens a full-width search field with results.
  • Follows your admin color scheme (Light, Midnight and the rest).
  • Configurable: choose which sources are searched, restrict post types, and set results per group, minimum query length, typing delay and the keyboard shortcut.
